newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Just one-night after being involved in an all-in brawl including 40 players during game two of Friday night's double-header between the Melbourne Monarchs and Adelaide Giants, Monarchs veteran Phil Dale became the first baseball pitcher to win 50 games in FAI Cup history. Page 20.

Following calls for sailing to become more exciting for the Sydney 2000 Olympics, the International Sailing Federation has included the Australian-designed 49er - a 4.9 metre long, two person, twin trapeze skiff created by Julian Bethwaite - in the regatta. Page 20.

Brad Jones, driving his four-wheel drive Audi A4, which was well-suited to the damp track, wrapped up the BOC Gases Australian 2-litre super touring car championship at Sydney's Oran Park Raceway with two wins from two starts on Saturday night. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian rugby union coach Greg Smith strongly indicated last night that, despite an encouraging Test win against the Scottish team, he will be opting for widespread changes in the lineup for the Wallabies' next international against Ireland at Lansdown Road on November 23. Page 26.

Australian Rugby League chief executive John Quayle says he believes Optus Vision's funding package has secured the immediate future of the ARL's 12-team competition and he says he will volunteer to resign at an ARL board meeting today to make way for thenew leadership he believes is necessary to administer the competition. Page 27.

Thanks to a 20th-minute goal by Michael Curcija, the Australian Olyroos Olympic soccer team won a two-match series in Johannesburg against their South African counterparts with a 1-1 draw at FNB Stadium on Sunday. Page 28.
THE AGE

Despite several advance death notices over the weekend, wicketkeeper Ian Healy will appear in his 81st Test on Friday week - as Australian vice captain in the Frank Worrell Trophy Test series. Page Sports 5.

England A crashed from 3/122 to be all out for 151 after Test leg-spinner Peter McIntyre ripped through their batting line in a sensational 21-ball session to put South Australia back on the road to victory in the four-day cricket match at Adelaide Oval ysterday. Page Sports 7.

Trainer Lee Freedman yesterday confirmed Melbourne Cup runner-up Count Chivas would not be racing again until the International Vase over 2,400 metres at Sha Tin on December 8. Freedman also outlined Hong Kong plans for Poetic King and said he is looking to the west with Storm, who will run the Perth Cup on New Year's Day. Page Sports 9.
HERALD SUN

Magic co-captain Darren Lucas, 30, met with coach Brian Goorjian last week and was offered a non-playing, marketing-type role. The decision has been left with Lucas to either accept the role or play on for his 12th basketball season with the club. Page 78.

Peter Hayes, last season's premier horse trainer, zoomed back into the spotlight with a treble on Final Day at Flemington after a luckless start to the spring carnival. Hayes is currently the leading VRC carnival trainer, with his stables gaining 20 wins n the past two weeks. Page 76.

Following the Encosta de Lago affair, when the colt was allowed to contest the Stutt Stakes at Moonee Valley despite registering high bicarb levels pre-race, the Australian Equine Veterinary Association will this week urge that legal bicarb levels not be reduced. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Despite scoring an unbeaten 150 against Victoria yesterday and making a significant contribution to the New South Wales side, Michael Bevan is still being looked upon cautiously as a Test cricketer, largely due to a perception that he cannot score against pace. Page 31.

Lanky Queensland pace bowler Brendan Creevey came tantalisingly close to a Mercantile Mutual sign during yesterday's Mercantile Mutual Cup cricket match against Tasmania - a direct hit on the sign would have won Creevey A$160,000 in prize money. Page 31.

Soccer referee Simon Micallef was the centre of controversy last night after awarding two crucial penalties to Sydney United in a dramatic Ericsson Cup match against UTS Olympic at Edensor Park which saw United win 2-1 before a crowd of 11,381. Page 30.
-- Reuters Sydney Newswroom 61-2 373-1800
